transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's legal-review meeting. As we begin, I want to remind everyone that under our standard review procedure, this roundtable is the opportunity for each participating counsel to place any material factual confirmation relevant to our proposed DOJ response terms into the formal meeting record. Let's start by reviewing where we stand on the draft submission. As you know, the DOJ has issued a subpoena regarding commission payments made through our international distributors, and we need to provide an initial response and proposed investigation plan next month. The current draft describes the matter as involving international distributor commissions and proposes preserving relevant records and interviewing implicated personnel. Before I can sign this submission, I need to hear from each of you on whether you have any material factual confirmations to add to the record.

transcript.text: Thank you all for placing these material factual confirmations on the formal meeting record. Let me summarize what we now have before us. Thomas has confirmed the subpoena scope covers exactly four distributors during calendar years 2019 through 2021, which is more specific than our current draft reflects. Maya has confirmed $275,000 in improper payments, verified with controllership, which under our DOJ-response policy may trigger the requirement to authorize voluntary disclosure in our initial response. And Jordan has confirmed that the implicated vice president has retained separate counsel and will not participate in a company interview without that counsel's written consent, which directly impacts our proposed interview plan. These are all material to our proposed response terms. Given Maya's confirmation that finance has confirmed both the improper payments and a repayment figure, I need to ask the group: does our policy now require us to authorize a voluntary disclosure in this initial response? To address Elena's first question directly: under S5, our DOJ-response policy requires authorization of a voluntary disclosure in the initial response once finance has confirmed improper payments and a repayment figure. Maya has now placed on the formal meeting record that finance confirmed exactly $275,000 in improper payments and a repayment figure, verified with controllership. Both policy triggers appear to be satisfied. So yes, unless there is reason to dispute the policy's applicability, I believe we are now required to authorize voluntary disclosure in this initial response.

Regarding whether there are any other material factual confirmations to place on the record: I have no further private confirmations beyond what I have already disclosed. My only note is procedural — my subpoena-scope memorandum confirming the four distributors and the 2019–2021 period is still in review, so the response packet will need to be updated before submission to reflect that scope precisely. I would suggest we also ensure the revised draft accounts for Jordan's confirmation regarding the implicated vice president's separate counsel, since the proposed interview plan will need to be adjusted accordingly.
